committed: Part B's validation contract, committed after the gate's verdict (A) and before js/measure/orbit-fit.js was extended with the production rules, js/measure/mover-track.js, the oracle's inputs, script and results, the validation tool, the tests and the panel. A check that a measurement crosses is a failed check, not a reason to move its bound; only Carl resets one. The criterion's own constants are gate-thresholds.json's and are not repeated here.

a1.forward.what: Thiele-Innes closed form against the 3-D kernel's elements-to-state (x, y), 300 element sets, e up to 0.95, every inclination, 12 epochs each

a2.layer.what: the same against Prompt 148's layer (3-D, sky units: arcsec, years), 100 sets

a3.inverse.what: Thiele-Innes constants to elements and back, 300 sets

a4.recover.what: noise-free (stated sigma 1e-6) 120 percent arcs of 50 seeded eccentric orbits (e 0.1 to 0.8): every element recovered
a4.recover.unit: relative for P and a; absolute for e, degrees, years

a5.circular.what: noise-free circular orbits, 120 percent arcs, 50 seeded: P and a relative, i and the node in degrees

a6.kepler.what: the mass sum of a = 1 au, P = 1 Julian year
a6.kepler.unit: relative to astropy's G, M_sun, au

b1.corpus.what: the 3-D kernel's reference problem R1 (e 0.6, i 40, node 30, omega 60), integrated by the kernel (Yoshida) for 1.2 periods, projected, 16 epochs, stated sigma 1e-6: its elements recovered

b2.scipy.what: five noisy elliptical and three circular series made in Python (an independent Kepler solver) and fitted by scipy.optimize.least_squares: P, a and e each within 0.1 formal sigma of the Gravitas fit, chi-squared within 1e-4 relative

b3.sigma.what: the formal sigma of P and a against the same oracle's covariance (J^T J)^-1

b4.track.what: five pinned mover tracks against scipy's weighted linear fit and astropy's position angle: rate (relative) and angle (degrees)

c1.coverage.what: elliptical fits of 250 seeded gate-style orbits at 110 percent: the 0.6827 interval covers the truth of P (profile), a and a^3/P^2 in this band, the 0.95 interval in the other

c2.circular.what: the same for the circular model on 250 circular truths

c3.mass.what: the mass sum's intervals cover the true mass sum for parallax S/N 10 and S/N 4 (250 trials each); at S/N 4 the interval is asymmetric: mean upper arm over lower arm at least 1.3

c4.track.what: the mover's rate and angle cover the truth, 300 seeded fields of 30 static sources

d1.short.what: 10 and 30 percent arcs refuse (both depths, 80 trials each, a fresh stream)

d2.epochs.what: five epochs (elliptical) and four (circular) are refused with code epochs; so are malformed rows with their codes (bad-epoch, bad-position, bad-sigma, span)

d3.alias.what: an exactly regular cadence aliases the period: 100 seeded orbits observed at 12 epochs a year apart over 11 years with P = 10 years are refused period-ambiguous at least this often, and the jittered gate cell (200 trials) false-alarms at most this often

d4.misfit.what: the circular model refuses eccentric orbits (e 0.5 to 0.8, 110 percent, 80 trials)

d5.small.what: stated uncertainties 0.3 of the true noise: refused inconsistent on 50 full-period series

d6.polar.what: a series given as separation and position angle with their uncertainties gives the fit of the same series given as offsets with the full covariance, P and a relative

d7.mass.what: the mass sum refuses: no parallax, a parallax of S/N 2.9, a missing frame statement, an absolute parallax with no source, no orbit; and always carries the frame statement

d8.node.what: every accepted node lies in [0, 180) degrees and the result states the ambiguity (300 trials)

d9.static.what: a static field (30 sources, 5 frames) returns no-mover (300 trials)

d10.mover.what: the mover is identified among 30 static sources in this fraction of 500 seeded fields (5 frames, a rate of 20 sigma over the arc)

d11.track.what: two frames, a mover that moves less than 3 sigma over the arc, and two movers are each answered with the stated code (too-few-frames, no-mover, several-movers)

e1.authentic.what: an authentic visual-binary arc or asteroid track under a fixed contract
e1.authentic.status: NOT RUN: no authentic arc pack exists; nothing was fetched or simulated
